summary_for_children: An-Nahl is the surah of the bee. It shows Allah's blessings in bees, honey, milk, rain, the sea, birds and animals, and asks us to be grateful.
environment_concept: A valley of blessings: rounded cliffs and a tree with bees' homes and wooden hives (16:68), honey jars in different colours (16:69), a pasture with a fold and a barn (16:5-6, 16:66), a lagoon with a boat and pearl shells (16:14) and birds held up in the sky (16:79). No person is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: Flower meadows, cliffs and trees with hives, a stream, grazing animals, birds in the sky, and a coast.

areas.name: Hive Cliffs
areas.description: Bees making homes in mountains and trees.

areas.name: Honey Spring
areas.description: Honey of different colours in the combs.

areas.name: Coast of Ornaments
areas.description: A coast with shells and pearls.

activities.name: Follow the bee
activities.description: Tap the flower where the bee sits; it flies on to the next, and after five flowers it goes home to the hive.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Count the blessings
activities.description: Collect blessings around the valley and learn they cannot all be counted.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Bring the flock home
activities.description: Bring the sheep into the round fold and the cows into the barn for the evening (16:6).
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: The narrator reads each ayah when a blessing is found.
learning_objectives: Describe what the Quran says about bees

status.playable_environment: first version built: its own scene (hive cliffs, honey jars, pasture, lagoon, birds) with two hands-on activities in the scene
status.testing: checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL at 960x600; not tested on phones or real GPUs
status.tested_by: automated screenshots of the scene and the in-scene activities

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.
